sound: Checked and sound: screensOf statuses (not-run, failed, partial and incomplete never read as clear; clearScreens comes from the screens), related-party screening via state.screened, screenedOk and screenFailed (field names match deepCheck.js), coverage of partly answered and not run sources, the not-covered list naming state registers, byEmployer (needs two records or a date span, serious records only hinted), the word-only count in the screens, the identity note when no record ties the person to the company, totals matching their lists, and cited leak confirmations. roleStart and orgFounded are written by no source (dead path).

findings.title: A confirmed criminal record vanishes from red flags when its headline does not name the person
findings.scenario: Confirmed press record, high severity. Title: 'Fintech startup CEO pleads guilty to wire fraud'. Quote: 'Jane Roe, founder and CEO of Zetafold, pleaded guilty...'. Result: no red flag, no namesake entry, seriousRecords 0, so the summary reads '0 red flags'. Real r9 Zhang run: confirmed medium Forbes record #2 about the China data allegations is dropped the same way.
findings.fix: Use aboutThem only to filter encyclopaedia or roundup pages (isWikiOther, data.wikiKind). Otherwise also accept a record whose quote names the person in full (subject.hasName) in the sentence that reports the serious event. Never drop a confirmed or likely serious record from every list: if it fails the test, keep it as a red flag marked 'mentioned in passing'.
findings.evidence: zzReview test A: totals.redFlags 0, seriousRecords 0. r9/jack-zhang-airwallex rebuilt: record 2 is confirmed, medium, not flagged.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. A confirmed high-severity press record, headline 'Fintech startup CEO pleads guilty...' with a quote naming Jane Roe, gives redFlags 0 and seriousRecords 0. aboutThem (line 822) tests only the title. Zhang r9 #2 (confirmed, medium) is also absent from every list.
findings.betterFix: Have aboutThem reject only when no sentence of the quote names the person (subject.hasName) together with the event (eventOf on that sentence), or when isWikiOther is true. If a confirmed or likely serious record still fails, keep it as a red flag marked 'mentioned in passing' rather than dropping it from every list.

findings.title: Acquittals, dismissals and pardons never attach to their matter, so the matter stays high with no outcome
findings.scenario: DOJ 'Jane Roe indicted on wire fraud charges' (2021-02, high), then 'Jury acquits Jane Roe' (2022-06). finding.js grades exculpatory records low and sets data.outcome. The report only groups medium or high records, and only within 31 days and one event tag. Result: a high red flag with no outcome. Milton r9: the 'Trump pardons' record is its own red flag, and the sentencing flag has no pardon.
findings.fix: After building matters, scan every tied record that has data.outcome, whatever its severity or date, and attach it to the matter it ends. Match on the same person, a shared docket or distinctive headline words, and a later date. Then lower the matter's severity for acquitted or dismissed (as finding.js does) and show the outcome.
findings.evidence: zzReview test B: redFlags[0] has severity high and no outcome. Rebuilt r9 Milton: no red flag carries an outcome; #10 'Trump pardons...' is a separate high flag.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. finding.js grades an acquittal 'low', so it never enters serious, and the indictment flag stays high with outcome null. In rebuilt Milton, the pardon is its own flag (#10, event tag 'pardon'), and sentencing flag #1 carries no outcome.
findings.betterFix: After the matters are built, attach every tied record with data.outcome (any severity) that is dated later to a red flag of the same whoOf and a compatible event (charges, conviction or sentence), matched by docket or shared headline words. Pardon matters fold into the conviction or sentence matter. Lower the severity for acquitted or dismissed, as gradeByOutcome does.

findings.title: Grouped page takes the severity of a name-only copy, so a benign confirmed page becomes a high red flag
findings.scenario: Page reader (confirmed, info): 'Jane Roe is the founder and CEO of Zetafold'. Web-search snippet of the same URL (possible, high): 'John Doe was convicted of fraud'. groupPages keeps the confirmed lead and gives it the highest severity in the group. Result: red flag #1 'Zetafold team', high, quoting a benign bio line. Another person's matter is pinned on the founder.
findings.fix: Take severity only from members tied at least as strongly as the lead (never from a 'possible' copy). When a tied member is more severe, make that member the lead, so the quote shown supports the flag.
findings.evidence: zzReview test C: redFlags [{t:'Zetafold team', sev:'high'}], copiesMerged 1. Milton r9: #13 Wikipedia 'Career' was raised from info to high by a copy.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. Line 569 takes the maximum severity across the group, including a 'possible' copy. The result is the 'Zetafold team' red flag, high, quoting a benign bio line.
findings.betterFix: Compute severity only from members whose TIE_ORDER is at least the lead's. If a tied member is more severe, it becomes the lead so the quote shown supports the flag. A severe 'possible' copy stays listed in alsoIn and never raises the group.

findings.title: One matter splits into many red flags (Milton: 35 red flags) when reports are undated, dated to the year only, or worded differently
findings.scenario: Rebuilt r9 Trevor Milton report: totals.redFlags is 35. Separate flags for the sentencing (#1, plus undated Reddit #54 and #55), the conviction (#32 dated 2022-10-19; #40 'Guilty of Defrauding Investors' 2022-10-14; Wikidata #3 and #4 dated '2022'), and the charges (#6; Reddit #56). The cause: undated records become 'single|id', year-only dates key as '2022', and 'Guilty of' matches no event.
findings.fix: Add a second pass that merges a tied serious record into an existing tied matter with the same event tag when they share at least one distinctive headline word. Treat an undated or year-only record as compatible with any window in its year. Add a bare '\bguilty\b' to the conviction pattern. Add a test asserting Milton has fewer than 12 red flags.
findings.evidence: Rebuilt r9/trevor-milton-nikola.json with the current buildReport: 35 red flags; per-flag titles and dates were printed and inspected.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. Rebuilt r9 Milton gives 35 red flags. The conviction is split across #3, #4 (year-only), #32, #40 ('Guilty of' matches no event), #30 and #14; the sentencing across #1, #54 and #55 (undated); the charges across #6 and #56.
findings.betterFix: Add 'guilty' to the conviction tag. In dateWindows and matterKey, let undated or year-only tied records of a RARE_EVENT for the same whoOf join that event's single window, or the window in their year when there is one. Merge only on rare events, not on lawsuits. Add a regression test that caps Milton's flags.

findings.title: A product launch year becomes the founding year, and the company's own domain is relabelled 'by an earlier holder'
findings.scenario: No founding fact in companyFacts. A confirmed record says 'Zetafold launched its bill pay product in 2022'. A domain-history record shows zetafold.com registered 2019-03-02. Result: the domain record is retitled 'first registered 2019-03-02, by an earlier holder (Zetafold was founded in 2022)' and taken off the timeline. That is a false statement about the company, and the brief will not let 'what checks out' rest on it.
findings.fix: Drop 'launched' and 'started' from the regex, or require the company itself as their object ('Zetafold was launched in', 'started Zetafold in'), never 'Zetafold launched <something>'. Require two agreeing records before marking a domain as an earlier holder's.
findings.evidence: zzReview test H printed 'zetafold.com: first registered 2019-03-02, by an earlier holder (Zetafold was founded in 2022)'.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. 'Zetafold launched its bill pay product in 2022' sets foundedYear to 2022, and the zetafold.com 2019 record is retitled 'by an earlier holder' and taken off the timeline.
findings.betterFix: In the first regex, allow only '<Co> was (founded|started|launched|incorporated|established)' or '<Co>, founded in'. Never allow '<Co> launched <object>'. Require two agreeing records, or a profile or companyFacts year, before marking a domain as an earlier holder's.

findings.title: A real title change on the person's own LinkedIn is dropped when the profile address has the usual numeric suffix
findings.scenario: Archived change record (likely), field 'headline', page linkedin.com/in/jane-roe-4b2a17, before 'CTO at Paribus', after 'CEO at Zetafold'. ownPage needs a path segment exactly equal to a slug candidate ('jane-roe'), and a headline never contains the full name. Result: claimChanges is empty.
findings.fix: In ownPage, also accept a segment that starts with a slug candidate followed by '-' and an alphanumeric suffix (or digits) on profile hosts such as linkedin.com/in. Alternatively, accept CLAIM_FIELDS changes on a record already graded confirmed or likely when the page is a profile page.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. A likely headline change on linkedin.com/in/jane-roe-4b2a17 gives claimChanges 0: ownPage needs an exact slug match, and a headline does not name the person.
findings.betterFix: In ownPage, also accept a segment matching ^<slug>(-[a-z0-9]{2,12})?$ when it sits under linkedin.com/in or another profile path. A CLAIM_FIELDS change on a record already graded confirmed or likely can count as own.

findings.title: Real company news leaves the numbered report as 'word only' for an ordinary-word company
findings.scenario: Company 'Ramp', records graded 'company' by news search. These are moved out of the report into wordOnly: "Ramp's new AI agents take on expense fraud", 'Stripe and Ramp partner on bill pay', 'Inside Ramp: the spend management upstart'. 'Ramp raises...' and 'Ramp acquires...' are kept. This thins the company picture the owner complained about.
findings.fix: In ordinaryWordOnly, demote to possible and keep the record numbered, rather than removing it as word-only, when the text has business context (a possessive followed by a product word, 'X and Ramp partner', a fintech or startup noun nearby). Move only records with an explicit non-company use (a boat ramp, 'ramp up') to wordOnly. Or widen names.js companyMention for possessives and 'and <Company>' partnerships.
findings.evidence: zzReview test J: wordOnly listed those three headlines next to 'Boat ramp closed' and 'Ramp up production'.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. 'Ramp's new AI agents...', 'Stripe and Ramp partner...' and 'Inside Ramp: the spend management upstart' go to wordOnly next to 'Boat ramp closed'. They are still listed with a reason, so nothing is silent, but the company picture thins.
findings.betterFix: Widen names.js companyMention, shared with the identity matcher so the two still agree, to cover a possessive followed by a noun, '<Org> and <Co> partner', and 'Inside <Co>:'. Do not special-case report.js.

findings.title: A judge 'sanctioning' a party outranks a criminal conviction in red-flag order
findings.scenario: Two tied records: 'Jane Roe convicted of securities fraud' (high, 2022) and 'Judge sanctions Jane Roe over discovery abuse in Zetafold contract suit' (medium, 2020). The headline word 'sanctions' gives weight 6, above conviction's 5, so the discovery sanction is listed first. Any tied report in `more` that mentions 'sanctions' (Russia sanctions, for example) lifts its matter the same way.
findings.fix: Give weight 6 only from the source or category (LIST_SOURCES, category 'sanctions', a debarment source). In headlines, count only list-specific wording ('sanctions list', 'OFAC', 'sanctioned by the Treasury', 'debarred'), not a bare 'sanction(s|ed)'.
findings.evidence: zzReview test D: redFlags order [#2 'Judge sanctions...', #1 'convicted...'].
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. 'Judge sanctions Jane Roe over discovery abuse' (medium) is listed ahead of 'Jane Roe convicted of securities fraud' (high), because a bare 'sanctions' in a headline gives weight 6.
findings.betterFix: Keep the weight-6 floor from LIST_SOURCES and category 'sanctions'. In headlines, match only list wording (OFAC, 'sanctions list', 'sanctioned by the Treasury', debarred, wanted list). A bare 'sanction(s|ed)' falls to the lawsuit weight.

findings.title: Every report of one company matter gets its own timeline row
findings.scenario: Five news records of one lawsuit against the company (match company, litigation, 2023-05-01 to 05-05) become one company matter, but the timeline lists all five. coverageOfFlag holds only red-flag members; company matters and 'if right person' members are not excluded. The duplicates also take up the 60-row cap.
findings.fix: Build coverageOfFlag from the 'more' lists of redFlags, companyMatters and ifRightPerson, and put each matter's lead on the timeline once.
findings.evidence: zzReview test E: companyMatters has 1 entry; the timeline shows 5 rows of the same suit.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. Five reports of one company lawsuit form one company matter, but the timeline has five rows, because coverageOfFlag reads only redFlags.more.
findings.betterFix: Build coverageOfFlag from the more lists of redFlags, companyMatters, ifRightPerson and possibleNamesake. Also add the companyMatters and ifRightPerson leads once, so each matter is one timeline row.
